title: Cranachan
subtitle: Toasted oatmeal, cream, raspberries, and whisky
excerpt: Toasted rolled oats folded through softly whipped double cream with honey, Scotch whisky, and fresh raspberries. Scotland's most elegant and effortless dessert.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cranachan is a traditional Scottish harvest festival dessert, historically made after the oat harvest in August with freshly milled oatmeal, cream, and seasonal soft fruit. The name derives from the Gaelic 'cream chrannaich'. Raspberries are the classic fruit; the Scottish climate produces some of the finest raspberries in the world, with Perthshire in particular renowned for its raspberry crop. The whisky is Scotch, traditionally a single malt from the Highlands. The dish is typically served deconstructed, with each component in separate bowls at the table so guests can assemble it to their taste.

content.text: Toast the oats in a dry pan until golden and nutty: this is what distinguishes cranachan from a plain fool. Whip the cream to soft peaks only; stiff cream will be cloying. Fold everything together lightly so the colours remain distinct. The dessert is best assembled just before serving so the oats keep their crunch.
Toast the oats in a dry frying pan over medium heat, stirring frequently, for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and smelling nutty. Tip onto a plate to cool.
Whip the cream to soft peaks. Fold in the honey and whisky.

Reserve a handful of raspberries for decoration. Lightly crush the remaining raspberries with a fork. Fold the crushed raspberries and most of the toasted oats into the cream, keeping it slightly swirled rather than fully mixed.
Spoon into glasses or bowls. Top with the reserved raspberries and the remaining toasted oats. Serve at once.
